---
title: Mirrors, deploys and CI
description: Ship static apps next to the docs, deploy to Cloudflare Workers, and get a preview URL for every pull request.
---

This page covers three parts of the template:

- **Mirrors** copy plain HTML/JS folders (a studio, demo pages, your library's `src/`) into the site unchanged.
- **Cloudflare Workers** serves the built site as static assets, for free on the Workers free plan.
- **GitHub Actions** checks every PR, gives it a preview URL, and deploys to production when you push a tag.

## Mirrors

A mirror serves a folder from disk under a URL prefix, byte for byte. Astro never processes these files: no bundling, no HTML rewriting. Relative URLs inside them keep working, so `import '../src/x.js'` and `fetch('../examples/a.json')` behave as they do when you open the folder with any static server.

Declare mirrors in `site.config.ts`:

```ts
mirrors: [{ from: './example/apps', to: 'apps' }],
```

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `from` | Folder to mirror, relative to the site root. It may be outside the site: `'../'`, `'../../my-framework'`. |
| `to` | URL prefix. `'apps'` serves `from/hello/index.html` at `/apps/hello/`. Nested prefixes like `'pixel/src'` work, and several mirrors can share one prefix. |
| `include` | Optional globs, relative to `from`. If you set it, only matching paths are mirrored. |
| `exclude` | Optional globs, relative to `from`. Matching paths are skipped. |

Glob rules:

- `*` and `?` match within one path segment, `**` matches across segments, and `{a,b}` matches either option.
- A pattern that matches a folder covers everything in it, so `src` means the same as `src/**`.
- A pattern with no `/` is tested against every segment of the path, so `*.test.js` or `fixtures` match at any depth.

Some paths are never mirrored:

- dotfiles and dot-folders (`.git`, `.env`)
- `node_modules`
- the site's own folder, when `from` contains it

### Several folders under one prefix

Pixel Studio's tools load files from sibling folders: `studio/` imports `../src/...` and fetches `../examples/*.json` and `../docs/SPEC.md`. To keep those URLs working, mirror the repository root with an `include` list. The folders then stay siblings under one prefix:

```ts
// website/site.config.ts inside the pixel-studio repo
mirrors: [
  {
    from: '../',
    to: 'pixel',
    include: ['src', 'studio', 'demo', 'examples', 'figures', 'docs/*.md'],
    exclude: ['*.test.js'],
  },
],
// → /pixel/studio/, /pixel/demo/, /pixel/src/..., /pixel/docs/SPEC.md
```

If the site lives in its own repository, clone both repositories side by side and use `from: '../pixel-studio'`. CI can reproduce that layout; see [Build against a second repository](#build-against-a-second-repository).

### In dev and at build

- **`astro dev`** serves mirrored files straight from disk. They get the correct `Content-Type` (`.js`/`.mjs` as JavaScript, `.json`, `.md`, images, `.wasm`, fonts) and `Cache-Control: no-store`, so an edit shows up on the next reload. Mirrored pages don't live-reload. Folder URLs resolve to their `index.html`, and `/apps/hello` redirects to `/apps/hello/`. Paths that escape `from`, hidden files and excluded files fall through to Astro's 404.
- **`astro build`** copies the files into `dist/<to>/` after Astro finishes and logs a file count and total size for each mirror. The build fails if a mirrored file would overwrite a page the site builds itself. It also fails if `from` doesn't exist, and the error names the resolved path.

## Cloudflare Workers

The site deploys as a Worker with [static assets](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/) and no server code. The config is in `wrangler.jsonc`:

- **`name`**: change `example-project` to your project's name. It sets the URLs `https://<name>.<subdomain>.workers.dev` and `https://<alias>-<name>.<subdomain>.workers.dev` for previews. `<subdomain>` is your account's workers.dev subdomain.
- **`assets.not_found_handling: "404-page"`**: unknown URLs get `dist/404.html` with status 404.
- **`assets.html_handling: "auto-trailing-slash"`**: `/docs` redirects to `/docs/`, and `/page.html` is served at `/page`. This matches Astro's folder-style output. Relative URLs in mirrored apps resolve the same way as in dev.
- **`preview_urls: true`**: required for the per-PR preview aliases.
- **`compatibility_date`**: bump it on purpose, for example when you upgrade wrangler.

### Headers

`public/_headers` ends up in `dist/` and sets these headers:

- **Every response:** `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, and `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self'`. Only your own pages can frame the site. Inline module scripts, live examples and same-origin iframes keep working.
- **`/_astro/*`** (hashed bundles): `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`.
- **Everything else** (HTML, mirrored apps, the search index): the platform default, `public, max-age=0, must-revalidate` plus an ETag. Browsers revalidate on each load, so a deploy is visible at once, and unchanged files cost a 304.

The file also contains a commented-out stricter CSP that you can adopt once you know what your examples need. Set each header in only one rule: when two matching rules set the same header, the values are joined with a comma.

### Local commands

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run cf:dev` | Builds, then serves `dist/` with the real Workers runtime at `http://localhost:8787`. No account needed. Use it to check redirects, the 404 page and headers. |
| `npm run deploy` | Checks, builds and deploys to production. Run `npx wrangler login` first. |
| `npm run deploy:preview` | Checks, builds and uploads a preview version aliased to the current git branch. Pass `-- --alias name` to choose the alias. Production is untouched. |
| `npx wrangler deploy --dry-run` | Validates the config without credentials. |

## GitHub Actions

Two workflows live in `.github/workflows/`:

- **`ci.yml`** runs on every PR, on pushes to `main`, on `v*` tags and on manual runs. It runs `npm ci`, `astro check` and `astro build`, plus `npm run docs:check` if that script exists. Then it uploads `dist/` as an artifact and calls `deploy.yml`.
- **`deploy.yml`** is a reusable workflow that uploads the artifact. It doesn't rebuild.

| Event | Result | URL |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pull request | Preview version, plus a sticky PR comment that is updated on each push | `https://pr-<number>-<name>.<subdomain>.workers.dev` |
| Push to `main` | Preview version | `https://next-<name>.<subdomain>.workers.dev` |
| Tag `v*` | Production (`wrangler deploy`) | `https://<name>.<subdomain>.workers.dev` or your custom domain |
| Manual run with "production" ticked | Production, from the selected ref | as above |
| Manual run without "production" | Preview aliased to the branch name | `https://<branch>-<name>.<subdomain>.workers.dev` |

A preview never changes what production serves. The workflows skip previews, and still succeed, for PRs from forks, for Dependabot PRs, and whenever the Cloudflare secrets are not set. A run on a PR is cancelled when a newer push arrives. Production deploys are queued, never cancelled. The workflows ask for least-privilege permissions: `contents: read`, plus `pull-requests: write` only for the deploy job, which posts the comment.

Preview URLs are public. To restrict them, put [Cloudflare Access](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/applications/) in front of `*-<name>.<subdomain>.workers.dev`. Aliases are not deleted when a PR closes. Each new upload to an alias replaces the version it points to.

### Site in a subfolder

If the site is a `website/` folder inside the framework's repository, set the folder at the top of `ci.yml`:

```yaml
env:
  SITE_DIR: website
```

Workflows must stay in the repository root's `.github/`. Move them there from `website/.github/`.

### Build against a second repository

If the site has its own repository and mirrors files from the framework's repository (`from: '../pixel-studio'`), set:

```yaml
env:
  SOURCE_REPO: you/pixel-studio  # checked out next to this repository, under its own name
  SOURCE_REF: main               # branch, tag or SHA
```

CI checks out both repositories as siblings, in folders named after them, which matches a local layout of two clones side by side. If the source repository is private, add a read-only fine-grained token for it as the `SOURCE_REPO_TOKEN` secret.

## One-time setup

1. **Pick the name.** Set `name` in `wrangler.jsonc`, and set `url` in `site.config.ts` to `https://<name>.<subdomain>.workers.dev`, or to your custom domain.
2. **Create the Worker.** Run `npx wrangler login` and then `npm run deploy` once from your machine. This creates the Worker and enables its workers.dev URL. Pushing a `v*` tag after step 3 works too.
3. **Create an API token.** In the Cloudflare dashboard, go to **My Profile → API Tokens → Create Token** and use the **Edit Cloudflare Workers** template. If you'd rather create a custom token, it needs these permissions:
   - Account → **Workers Scripts: Edit**
   - Account → **Account Settings: Read**
   - User → **User Details: Read**
   - User → **Memberships: Read**
   - Zone → **Workers Routes: Edit**, only if you use a custom domain or routes, scoped to that zone

   Limit the token's account resources to your account.
4. **Add the GitHub secrets.** Under **Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → Repository secrets**, add:
   - `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`: the token from step 3
   - `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`: shown in the dashboard sidebar on **Workers & Pages**, or from `npx wrangler whoami`
   - `SOURCE_REPO_TOKEN`: optional, only for a private `SOURCE_REPO`
5. **Optional: protect production.** The workflows deploy into GitHub environments named `preview` and `production`. Add required reviewers to `production` under **Settings → Environments** to gate releases.

### Custom domain

The domain's zone must be on the same Cloudflare account.

1. Uncomment `routes` in `wrangler.jsonc` and put your hostname in:
   ```jsonc
   "routes": [{ "pattern": "docs.example.com", "custom_domain": true }]
   ```
2. Set `url` in `site.config.ts` to `https://docs.example.com`.
3. Deploy: push a `v*` tag, or run `npm run deploy`. Cloudflare creates the DNS record and certificate.
4. Optional: set `"workers_dev": false` so the site is only served on your domain. Preview URLs keep working, because they depend on `preview_urls`, not on `workers_dev`.
